title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Temporal Root Epoch, Compromise Horizon, and Recovery Extension
problem_statement: Trust in a root credential must be scoped over time. A credential that becomes compromised later should not automatically erase all prior history, while the same credential must not remain authoritative for new checkpoints after the credible compromise horizon.

new_primitives.ROOT_EPOCH_ID: Versioned period of root eligibility and quorum policy.
new_primitives.VALID_FROM_COORDINATE: First sequence/time coordinate at which a root epoch may attest.
new_primitives.VALID_UNTIL_COORDINATE: Last known or policy-bounded coordinate of eligibility.
new_primitives.COMPROMISE_HORIZON: Earliest defensible coordinate or interval at which trust in the credential becomes contested.
new_primitives.COMPROMISE_RECORD: Append-only record of evidence, uncertainty and affected trust domains.
new_primitives.RECOVERY_POLICY_ID: Separately bound policy for activating recovery credentials and creating a new epoch.
new_primitives.RECOVERY_DOMAIN_ID: Trust domain intentionally separated from routine operational signing where feasible.
new_primitives.RECOVERY_CHECKPOINT: First checkpoint of restored continuity, linked to last accepted pre-horizon checkpoint and compromise record.

temporal_validation.historical_attestation_before_horizon: Evaluate under the root registry and quorum policy valid at that historical coordinate, plus any later evidence that moves the compromise horizon earlier.
temporal_validation.unknown_compromise_time: Represent an interval; do not invent an exact instant.
temporal_validation.revocation_effect: Prospective trust removal plus explicit reassessment window, not silent deletion of historical records.

recovery_algorithm: stop new world-effect commits requiring contested trust
preserve all current state and alternate roots as forensic evidence
bound the compromise horizon from independent evidence
select last pre-horizon checkpoint with valid historical quorum and independent archival survival
activate recovery policy using a different trust domain where available
replay suffix events from independently checkable receipts
classify unresolved suffix as quarantined or contested
publish a recovery checkpoint chained to the compromise event

non_retroactivity.exception: Evidence that compromise existed earlier moves the horizon backward and reopens affected history.
non_retroactivity.reason: Trust history must reflect evidence about when authority was lost, not simply the date revocation was noticed.

terminal_failure_conditions: all ordinary and recovery trust domains plausibly compromised with no external evidence boundary
compromise horizon cannot be bounded enough to identify any admissible recovery root
implementation_tests: later root revocation does not silently delete pre-horizon receipts
post-horizon signature from revoked domain fails normal admission
uncertain compromise interval marks overlapping checkpoints contested
recovery starts from last admissible pre-horizon checkpoint rather than newest signed checkpoint
new root epoch references compromise record and prior accepted checkpoint
all-roots-compromised case returns evidence-insufficient rather than PASS
epistemic_boundaries: The exact compromise time may be unknowable.
Historical signature validity does not prove the signed claim was true about the world.
Recovery establishes bounded continuity under stated trust assumptions, not metaphysical identity.
canonical_lines: A broken key today does not automatically rewrite yesterday, but it must not be allowed to sign tomorrow as if nothing happened.
When the compromise horizon is uncertain, uncertainty belongs in the state.
